PullRequest.Title: sessions: use touch-sized mobile quick input metrics
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.

## Summary

Advanced mobile pickers such as Add Context / Files retain the shared quick-input
controller, but its compact row metrics do not match phone touch targets.
Stretching those rows in CSS leaves scrolling, clipping and hit areas out of sync.

- Add an optional minimum item height to the internal controller options and
  forward it to both virtualized list and tree delegates, including separators
  with actions. The isolated mobile entry chooses 44px; desktop defaults stay
  22px / 30px / 44px.
- Preserve the workbench factory's focus policy and Back keybinding while
  forwarding controller options.
- Give advanced mobile inputs the phone body font and minimum touch height.
  Remove the compact toolbar offset that clips full-height item actions.
- Keep shared filtering, multi-selection, item actions, and simple mobile
  sheets unchanged.

Independent fix for F4 in the mobile usability audit; not stacked on the other
mobile-fix drafts. Two independent read-only reviews found no blocking defect.
Added separator coverage following review.

## Validation

- `npm run gulp -- compile-client` — passed, zero errors.
- `npm run transpile-client` — passed for the final test changes.
- `node test/unit/browser/index.js --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/mobile/test/browser/mobileQuickInputService.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/quickinput/test/browser/quickinput.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/quickinput/test/browser/quickInputUtils.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/quickinput/test/browser/tree/quickInputTreeSorter.test.ts --browser chromium` — **96 passed**.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/mobile/test/browser/mobileQuickInputService.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/quickinput/test/browser/quickinput.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/quickinput/test/browser/quickInputUtils.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/quickinput/test/browser/tree/quickInputTreeSorter.test.ts` — **97 passed**.
- `npm run valid-layers-check` — passed.
- `git diff --check` and normal commit hygiene hooks — passed.
- `BUILD_SOURCEVERSION="$(git rev-parse HEAD)" npm run bundle-mobile` — passed
  unchanged policy at `142266976c12d6700d4592f2d5c59cbec96fee84`.

The mobile picker regression failed before the fix. Tests measure actual and
virtual row heights, row separation, scrolling to the last item, filtering,
selection, item actions, Back, and action-bearing separators. Desktop cases
assert the existing compact metrics.

| Measurement | gzip bytes | Unchanged limit |
|---|---:|---:|
| Initial | 6,308,857 | 7,000,000 |
| Main JavaScript | 5,702,291 | 6,400,000 |
| CSS | 242,905 | 275,000 |
| Runtime | 14,710,488 | 16,500,000 |
| Extensions | 712,868 | 800,000 |

Manual follow-up: open Add Context / Files at phone width, filter and scroll,
then exercise multi-selection and per-item actions. Verify the same flows in
the regular workbench remain compact.

Physical iOS/Safari, screen readers and live attachment submission were not
validated. No live account data was changed by these component tests.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open, filter, scroll, select, and invoke actions in mobile advanced quick-pick lists and quick trees, including action-bearing separators.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: First use lazily creates the shared controller and UI; supplied items are indexed before visible rows render. Filtering traverses the existing collection and updates the tree. Scrolling/reveal renders the viewport range. The diff changes numeric delegate heights to at least 44px and adjusts input/action CSS, without adding geometry measurements, filtering passes, or dynamic-height probing.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the saved quick-input position through storageService.get and JSON.parse.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One small saved-state read per controller creation, not per row or picker reopening.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same lazy controller constructor read and parsed the same saved position once.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous first-controller initialization; unchanged by the diff.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Apply widget dimensions and lay out the existing virtualized list/tree.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing layout invocations; DOM rows normally correspond to the viewport, approximately viewportHeight/44 on mobile. Collection insertion still evaluates one constant-time height delegate per inserted item.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same virtualized rendering and layout paths used 22px ordinary/tree rows, 30px separator rows, and 44px detail rows. The larger minimum does not increase viewport row cardinality.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Main-thread presentation and scrolling work. The diff adds no layout calls or read-after-write geometry loops.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N supplied items/tree nodes and query-change frequency; DOM rendering is viewport-based rather than all N items. Separators participate in the existing tree model.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous UI work on the browser thread; no new tasks, async fan-out, listeners, or independent controller instances. Existing owner disposal is unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The controller and its UI remain lazy and reused. Existing row-template recycling remains intact. No new cache, retained collection, negative-cache behavior, or invalidation policy is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced both height delegates through WorkbenchObjectTree to ListView's numeric size indexing and viewport rendering. Neither delegate introduces dynamic measurement.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No device profiling was performed; exact CSS/layout costs are not measured.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The added Math.max operations are constant-time, virtualization is preserved, and changed CSS does not introduce a repeated layout mechanism.

Scenarios.Scenario: Search files through the Add Context quick-access picker on mobile.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: AttachContextAction opens the existing Anything quick-access provider. File results depend on its existing search/cache path before being converted to quick-pick items; the changed controller only supplies row metrics to their presentation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Search workspace files through searchService.fileSearch, potentially crossing provider/process/remote boundaries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Cache loading has its existing grouped workspace search. A nonempty filename query normally makes one grouped search request, with a second sequential request only when a multipart query hits the result limit. Each request specifies maxResults=512. There is no request per rendered row.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical provider, query count, result limits, cancellation, and cache keys; row heights were smaller.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Result availability waits for search. Cache population is initiated separately; cold query execution uses the existing ThrottledDelayer, while a loaded cache permits direct query execution.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Stat candidate paths and resolve a successful candidate's parent to match filename casing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Absolute-path input checks one candidate. Relative input containing a path separator checks up to W workspace folders sequentially, with one parent resolve per successful file candidate. Ordinary filename queries do not enter the relative-path stat loop.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same path-dependent filesystem operations and concurrency occurred before this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Absolute-path checks precede fallback search; relative-path checks run alongside grouped file search and are awaited before merged results.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Query frequency and workspace size for grouped search; W workspace folders for relative-path checks, not the number of displayed file results.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing throttled cold-query scheduling; primary and conditional secondary searches are sequential, while relative-path checking runs alongside search. Relative workspace-folder stats are sequential. No new boundary concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: FileQueryCacheState retains compatible previous cache state while refreshing and disposes obsolete cache keys. Cold queries use the existing delayer; warm queries reuse the existing cache key. The diff does not alter successful, failed, or pending cache behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced AttachContextAction._show to AnythingQuickAccessProvider and inspected query grouping, cache ownership, result limits, and filesystem branches.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Workspace/provider latency and remote deployment details vary; none of their scheduling or cardinality changes in the diff.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: expensive search and filesystem paths are unchanged and are not newly invoked by the height option or CSS.

Scenarios.Scenario: Choose Files from Add Context and attach selected ordinary files.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: FileContextValuePick opens the existing file dialog, waits for selection, and resolves attachments before returning them. For ordinary non-image files the resolver stats each resource and constructs attachment metadata. Row sizing does not participate in attachment resolution.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One dialog invocation per explicit Files action, not per quick-input row or layout.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same explicit action opened the same dialog with multi-selection enabled.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: User selection must finish before attachments can be resolved.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Stat each selected ordinary file through fileService.stat.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One stat per selected ordinary file; the caller awaits resolution sequentially across selected resources.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical sequential attachment resolution and filesystem calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each selected attachment waits for its existing stat; no new work is moved onto this path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: S explicitly selected ordinary files, not all files visible in the picker.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing sequential resolution across S selected resources; unchanged by the diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The diff adds no attachment cache and does not change file-service/provider cache behavior. Controller reuse is independent of attachment resolution.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced the Files action and its ordinary-file resolver; changed lines only affect shared picker presentation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: File-dialog backend and local versus remote stat latency vary. Image-specific resolution is outside this ordinary-file scenario and is not changed by the PR.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression: dialog count, selected-file cardinality, and I/O scheduling are unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Use simple mobile one-shot pick and input bottom sheets.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Simple picks still await supplied items and activeItem, build the existing sheet, and resolve on selection. Sheet search remains locally filtered for this service. Inputs still invoke caller-provided validation on edits/acceptance. The new createController override is only used when the shared controller is requested.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: N supplied sheet choices and edit frequency; pre-existing local filtering is linear in N. Validation cost remains owned by the caller.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing sheet search uses 150ms debounce and cancellation/replacement of pending requests. Input validation retains its existing generation checks; no scheduling change.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new caches. Sheet listeners, pending search cancellation, timers, and row stores retain their existing lifetimes. Simple sheet use does not newly initialize the controller.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: inspected mobile routing, sheet search scheduling and cleanup, and the unchanged simple-input implementation. No direct subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network call is added on these paths.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Caller-supplied validation may perform external operations, but the diff changes neither its invocation frequency nor ordering.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. New quick-input-widget CSS selectors do not target the simple sheet fields, and simple-sheet routing is unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Use desktop quick picks and quick trees through the workbench factory.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing factory lazily creates and reuses a controller with the same focus policy and Back-keybinding callbacks. Omitted minimumItemHeight becomes zero, preserving desktop row sizes.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: N supplied entries and normal layout/filter events. Option spreading is constant-size controller-construction work, not per item.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing synchronous UI execution with unchanged provider scheduling; no new async work or boundary calls.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing controller/UI reuse and row recycling are unchanged; no new cache state or retained resources.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: compared the factory forwarding, constructor defaults, and all delegate branches against the deleted lines. Existing storage/layout boundaries are accounted for in the shared-controller scenario.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No measured desktop timing data; the changed default calculation preserves actual dimensions.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: desktop rows remain 22px/30px/44px for lists and 22px for trees; factory option forwarding adds no scaling work.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass across all nine changed files and every diff page against base 36e8c0289a5f29eae15a933263220d9895302ff6. Traced lazy controller ownership, virtualized rendering, layout/filter paths, mobile routing, representative file-search/attachment boundaries, cache behavior, and concurrency. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance regression found. The sizing correction is not independently established as a performance-regression fix, so no provenance report was warranted. Static review only; device-specific rendering duration remains unmeasured.
